attachments.insertion_landmark: lateral part of the inferior nuchal line

actions: rotates the head to the same side

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Forms the medial border of the suboccipital triangle. The suboccipital muscles have an exceptionally high muscle spindle density for their size, which is why they are treated as proprioceptive organs for head position as much as prime movers.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

trigger_points.location_description: Belly about 2 cm lateral to the midline, between the C2 spinous process and the occiput, palpated through semispinalis capitis.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Deep, poorly localised pain 'inside the head' from the occiput to the orbit and forehead on the same side, described as the whole side of the head or a deep retro-orbital ache that cannot be pinpointed.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Forward-head posture with craniocervical extension (looking up through bifocals, high screens), head-forward reading, occlusal posturing; satellite of trapezius, sternocleidomastoid, splenius and semispinalis trigger points.
trigger_points.notes: Suboccipital and temporal trigger points are found in 74% of migraineurs and relate to headache intensity/duration in chronic tension-type headache.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded head and neck muscle reference document (Simons DG, Travell JG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol 1, 2nd ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1999; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019)
